summary:
### TL;DR
- **GitHub-hosted runners will stop running ARM32 jobs on Linux and Windows by December 8, 2026.** Node 24 does not support ARM32, so this follows the end of node20 support. ([changelog](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-11-12-actions-for-arm32-linux-windows-retirement))
- Secret scanning now detects Cloudflare Access service tokens (`cloudflare_access_service_token`). ([changelog](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-11-12-secret-scanning-adds-a-detector-for-cloudflare))
- New docs guidance: keep the CodeQL action current. Old pinned versions can lose features when server-side flags are removed. ([docs](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/how-tos/find-and-fix-code-vulnerabilities/configure-code-scanning/configuring-advanced-setup-for-code-scanning))
- Each public monitoring alert now has its own URL that you can bookmark or share. ([changelog](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-11-12-public-monitoring-alerts-now-have-direct-links))

### Action required
- **ARM32 retirement on hosted runners. Deadline: December 8, 2026.**
  - Support for ARM32 job execution on Windows and Linux hosted runners ends by that date.
  - This includes native AArch32 user-space execution.
  - Find workflows that rely on ARM32 or AArch32 execution and migrate them before the deadline.
  - Source: [changelog](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-11-12-actions-for-arm32-linux-windows-retirement)
- **Pinned CodeQL action versions** (recommended, no fixed deadline).
  - If you pin `github/codeql-action` to a commit SHA or patch tag, keep it updated, for example with Dependabot.
  - Some features depend on server-side flags that may be removed over time, so stale versions can silently lose functionality.
  - Source: [docs](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/how-tos/find-and-fix-code-vulnerabilities/configure-code-scanning/configuring-advanced-setup-for-code-scanning)

### Security improvements
- **Cloudflare service token detection.** Secret scanning now detects `cloudflare_access_service_token`.
  - In public repositories, partner secrets are reported automatically to the issuer.
  - User secrets raise alerts in both public and private repositories.
  - Source: [changelog](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-11-12-secret-scanning-adds-a-detector-for-cloudflare)
- **Direct links to public monitoring alerts.** Click an alert number in the enterprise Public monitoring view to open it on its own page with a unique URL.
  - Available to GitHub Enterprise Cloud customers with GitHub Secret Protection or GitHub Advanced Security, at no extra cost.
  - Sources: [changelog](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-11-12-public-monitoring-alerts-now-have-direct-links), [docs](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/how-tos/view-and-interpret-data/analyze-organization-data/viewing-public-monitoring-alerts)

### Docs changes worth reading
- **Keeping the CodeQL action up to date.** This new section recommends referencing the action by major version tag (e.g., `v4`) to get bug fixes, features, and CodeQL CLI updates automatically. If you pin to a SHA or patch version for supply-chain reasons, you must keep that pin updated. ([docs](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/how-tos/find-and-fix-code-vulnerabilities/configure-code-scanning/configuring-advanced-setup-for-code-scanning))
- **AI Scan for repositories.** The docs now explain that enabling the org setting does not start any scans. After enabling it, you can start one-off scans of up to 20 repositories, or scan a single repository from its code scanning alerts page. ([concepts](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/concepts/code-scanning/ai-scan-for-repositories), [org settings](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/how-tos/secure-at-scale/configure-organization-security/establish-complete-coverage/configure-global-settings))
- **Check runs per check suite limit.** The limit is 50,000 check runs per suite. Per the commit title, the docs now state it cannot be raised; previously they said it could be raised via support ticket. ([docs](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/limits), [commit](https://github.com/github/docs/commit/92aee245f30e97a3fc88219aeae8938aacf338b1))
- **macOS runner queue times.** A note about queue times during high demand was added to the hosted runners and limits pages. The diff does not include the note's exact wording. ([runners](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/runners/github-hosted-runners), [limits](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/limits))

changelog.title: Actions for ARM32 Linux & Windows retirement
changelog.text: GitHub Actions hosted runners will be ending support for ARM32 job execution on Windows and Linux by 8th Dec 2026. This follows our end of support for node20 where Node 24 does not support ARM32. This includes the removal of support on hosted runners for native AArch32 User-space execution. Join the discussion within GitHub Community . The post Actions for ARM32 Linux & Windows retirement appeared first on The GitHub Blog .

changelog.title: Secret scanning detects Cloudflare service tokens
changelog.text: Secret scanning now detects Cloudflare service tokens. Detectors added Secret scanning now automatically detects the following new secret type in your repositories. Provider Secret type Cloudflare cloudflare_access_service_token Partner secrets are automatically reported to the secret issuer when found in public repositories through the secret scanning partnership program . User secrets generate secret scanning alerts when found in public or private repositories. Learn more Learn more about secret scanning and see the full list of supported secrets in our documentation. Let us know what you think in the community discussion . The post Secret scanning detects Cloudflare service tokens appeared first on The GitHub Blog .

changelog.title: Public monitoring alerts now have direct links
changelog.text: You can now access individual public monitoring alerts with a direct link to each alert. In your enterprise’s Public monitoring view, click an alert number to open the alert. You can use its URL to bookmark the finding or share it with teammates who have access. Public monitoring is available for GitHub Enterprise Cloud customers with GitHub Secret Protection or GitHub Advanced Security, at no additional cost. Learn more about viewing and managing public monitoring alerts , or share your feedback in the community discussion . The post Public monitoring alerts now have direct links appeared first on The GitHub Blog .
